# Tree Routing And Decoding

The model builds context from the leaves toward the root, then each requested
field decoder reads the context available along its schema path. For the
payment example, earlier transactions contribute history context, which the
root combines with the current amount and merchant to predict `disputed`.

This routing explanation was checked
against the [pinned 0.2.4 execution plan](https://github.com/relflow/relflow/blob/8d9d6cfd8ce22a7819c2b5392c710d4f2cbe1a7c/src/relflow/architecture/runtime.py).

## Context Moves Toward The Root

```{typst}
//| label: fig-mechanism-tree-routing
//| fig-alt: "A payment root contains amount, merchant, a repeated recent_transactions branch with days_ago, amount, and merchant, and the disputed prediction target. Transactions build local history context before the root combines it with the current payment."
//| fig-cap: "Connections show schema ownership. History builds context before the root combines it with the current payment; the disputed decoder reads that context."
#tree(node("payment", kind: "root", body: [Combines current payment and history.], children: (
  node("amount", type: "Number"),
  node("merchant", type: "Category"),
  node("recent_transactions", kind: "branch", repeated: true, body: [Builds history context.], children: (
    node("days_ago", type: "Number"),
    node("amount", type: "Number"),
    node("merchant", type: "Category"),
  )),
  node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean", body: [Supervised value hidden from input.]),
)))
```

Each active leaf first supplies a field representation with its presence
information. The runtime sends it to its owning branch. Branches execute from
the deepest level upward, so a parent receives representations from its nested
branches after those branches have encoded and reduced their own children.

For this payment model, the history branch processes its transaction fields
first. The root then processes the current payment fields and the history's
output. With more nesting, the same rule repeats at each level. Branches at one
depth form a group in the execution plan; this grouping describes dependencies,
without promising parallel execution.

The root is anonymous at `rf.Address()`. `payment` in the figure describes the
observation; it does not add an address prefix. For schema construction and
addresses, see [Model Tree](../../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd).

## A Decoder Reads Its Path

A target decoder receives the representations retained along its heritage:
the schema path through its ancestors to the field. A nested target can
therefore use both local branch context and broader root context. Decoding
starts after context has been built; it does not reconstruct the input tree
one parent prediction at a time.

Query pooling uses learned queries shaped for the target's coordinates. Where
sibling representations align with those coordinates, the decoder can also
condition those queries on sibling context. The field's decoder then produces
the datatype-specific answer, such as the Boolean output for `disputed`. See
the [pinned decoder implementation](https://github.com/relflow/relflow/blob/8d9d6cfd8ce22a7819c2b5392c710d4f2cbe1a7c/src/relflow/tensorfields/base.py).

`mask=True` keeps the supervised value out of the input while retaining its
coordinate for reconstruction. `embed=True` requests an exported contextual
representation and adds no reconstruction objective. These roles have their
own explanations in [Masking And Objectives](../../core-concepts/dynamic-masking.qmd)
and [Embeddings](../../core-concepts/embeddings.qmd).

## Read The Result

Prediction returns an Arrow table with a `predictions` column. The output
follows schema names and repeated field coordinates; it is not the runtime's
internal list of routed representations. Follow
[Read Predictions](../prediction-output.qmd) for one payment's output and its
state, content, and inference flag.

Continue with [Branch Summaries](branch-reduction.qmd) for the information passed
between levels, or [How Fields Interact](field-interactions.qmd) for the context
built inside each branch.
